steps.text: The nights spent up in the spire were always quiet, compared to the clamor of the city.
The cheers grow increasingly loud as elegantly dressed musicians leave one by one with their instruments in tow. She remains the last one in the vehicle.
'Don't be afraid, Viviana.' Someone walks over and holds her hand. 'Kazimierz and Leithanien aren't the same, but you'll get used to it.'
She nods obediently and follows the crowd out of the car.
Still, she subconsciously closes her eyes as the neon lights of the Grand Knight Territory pierce her vision.
She's never told this to anyone, but back then, it wasn't the strange new country she was so afraid of.
After all, her impression of Leithanien came solely from the window in her room, less than a square meter wide. It's hard to say that she knew the country all that well.
What she found so frightening was that the seemingly noisy evening outside might not actually be so different from the small slice of the night in her memories.
Viviana.
Are you alright, Viviana?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: ...Frau Löwenstein.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I'm reminded of when I first arrived in Kazimierz. Back then... you were holding my hand, just like now.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Your palms are all sweaty. What happened?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I... It's nothing. I just chatted with a strange woman.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: I stopped by Graf Josef's office earlier, but I only sensed your presence when I arrived here.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: She didn't do anything to me, and showed no hostility either. I think she simply came for the paintings too.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Right, about the paintings...

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Hmm.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Ah, I'm sorry. Should I describe what they look like for you?

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: No, please avert your eyes from them.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Is there something wrong with them?

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Their odor.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: During the Witch King's reign, people were far more enthusiastic about Originium research than they are today. The casters, or should I say, artists on the side of the Witch King, saw it as more than just an energy source, or a material for conducting Arts.

spans.text: During the Witch King's reign, people were far more enthusiastic about Originium research than they are today. The casters, or should I say,
on the side of the Witch King, saw it as more than just an energy source, or a material for conducting Arts.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: They believed that Originium was another form of flesh and blood, and could serve as a medium for the soul.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: So you're saying, the black substance on the paintings is...

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Refined Originium crystals mixed with the artist's blood.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: It sounds like this 'exhibit' was rather well thought out.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Go cover up the paintings. Use the heaviest fabric you can, and be sure not to touch the frames.

steps.name: Gendarmerie
steps.text: Understood.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: I think the two of you should leave as soon as possible. The intruder has yet to be found, so the art gallery isn't safe.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: It's not just us who are in danger.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: The people living in this city... everyone needs to be alerted.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: The ones who caused Frau Seemann's death and used her to paint these works are most likely...

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Please, don't say the name.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Frau Löwenstein, Das Kaiserinnensfest is just around the corner, and you know better than anyone that Their Majesties wouldn't want to see Zwillingstürme fall into chaos.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Which is why we're here.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: ...Can you at least inform the people who came to the gallery earlier?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I worry for their mental state after seeing such horrific paintings.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: How kind of you.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: I've already dispatched people to check on the crowd who came today, so don't worry. I also hope they didn't get too close a look.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: ...Herr Vizegraf.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I don't want Frau Seemann to have died a dubious death.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: She was a guest at His Majesty's spire on that night twenty-three years ago, correct?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: She witnessed firsthand the fall of the Witch King, and the birth of our national heroes.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: ...I see.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: But what of it?

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Believe me, meine Dame, on that night, the youths congregating before that pitch-black spiral spire weren't the only ones thirsting for dawn to break... There were many, many more.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Moreover, most of them did not become the heroes they thought they would be, the brave souls delivering Leithanien's rebirth.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Now, I've gotten an update on my intruder, so if you'll excuse me.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: He's right. That night changed many things, but change... isn't necessarily good.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: The remnants may have planned Frieda Seemann's death as punishment for 'betraying' the Witch King, or maybe it was meant to send a signal announcing a major move.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: ...Did they kill my father for the same reason?

steps.name: Strange Voice From A Sculpture
steps.text: Meine Dame.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Shh.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Let me finish listening to this piece.

steps.name: Strange Voice From A Sculpture
steps.text: It's just the performance of a vagrant.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: He was playing the same melody this morning, but now with such a different mood.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: He expected the gallery to be full of visitors today, and was planning to have a sandwich for dinner with an extra bratwurst to go.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: But now he realizes that he might have to go to bed hungry, yet again.

steps.name: Strange Voice From A Sculpture
steps.text: Did you... probe into his mind with your Arts?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: No need for that. Haven't you noticed? The homeless gentleman is telling his story right now through his music, again and again. All I'm doing is paying attention.

steps.name: Strange Voice From A Sculpture
steps.text: ...His story has nothing to do with us, though. The next stage has already been set.
The stone sculpture by the flowerbed ceases to speak.
Instead of words, it now hums a tune, smooth and deep, from the vibrating structure within.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: You Leithanians really do fancy your sound-producing sculptures.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: They give a 'perfect' performance every time, but it lacks soul... just like the people trapped in the spires.
Arturia gently blows a petal towards the mouthpiece of a large musical instrument carved into a sculpture.
It rises and falls with the airflow, and the formerly uniform tune immediately changes, ever so slightly.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Much better.

steps.name: Gendarmerie
steps.text: Captain! We were so close to catching the intruder, but he suddenly disappeared on us!

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Are the roads outside still under lockdown?

steps.name: Gendarmerie
steps.text: Ja. He can't possibly have grown wings and flown over us, can he?

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Wings... heh, hard to say.

steps.name: Gendarmerie
steps.text: We... We've really let you down, Captain. Encountering such a setback just when you're just about to—

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: It's fine, Pym. Go find Graf Josef and tell him what's going on with the art gallery.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Incidentally... I haven't heard the sound of gunfire in a long, long time.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: I've never been qualified to wield one, even back in my Laterano days. But I can assure you that the wands we use in the Gendarmerie hit just as hard and true.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: So, before my men return, you'd best put away your firearm... and your other weapons.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: And then, explain—

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: What business brings a Sankta like you to Zwillingstürme?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Loris Bordin.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Oh? You recognize me.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Former Lateran citizen. Twenty-eight years ago, you came to Leithanien from Laterano and joined the Gendarmerie.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Twenty-three years ago, the Twin Empresses conferred you the title of Vizegraf, and afterwards you became the commander of the Gendarmerie, a position you still occupy to this day.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: ...Hah. I was counting on you to introduce yourself first.

spans.text: ...Hah. I was counting on you to introduce

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I require your assistance in bringing an important fugitive back to Laterano.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Fugitive?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Her name is Arturia.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: ...Now I remember.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: You're that... executor from the Curia's Fifth Tribunal, the Notarial Hall's Fe... Fe... I'm sorry, the list of titles on your sign-offs is always so long, I can't recall your actual name.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Federico Giallo.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Our dealings are considered international affairs, so according to protocol, signatures are to be as meticulous as possible.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Ha... haha... The dozen or so letters you sent to me are still—

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Twenty-seven letters.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Did you read them properly? Did you even open them at all?

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: *ahem!* How could I... Anyway, you wrote all those letters over the past few years, and even personally came to Lethanien, just to hunt down this fugitive, yes?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: She has been active in Leithanien for many years now. I have reason to believe she is related to numerous unusual cases occurring here, including many of the cases you're currently working on.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: First it was His late Majesty, and now a fugitive from Laterano... When it rains, it pours, I suppose.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Do you require a briefing on the suspect and her situation from the very beginning? Alternatively, you may read any of the letters I sent you.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Ah...

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Reverend Executor, if I could have just a moment.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: ...Baron Lukas. Please go ahead.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Those... violent thugs disturbing the peace on the streets are back?

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Alright, I got it. I'll send men over right away.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Uh... Of course, absolutely. I'll be there in person. Please rest assured that the Gendarmerie will keep you safe and maintain Leithanien's untarnished glory.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: ...As you can see, I'm a very busy man.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I disagree. The social status of the informant should not be a criteria in determining the priority of your tasks.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Look, we're not in Laterano. Speaking of which, you're not allowed to freely fire your gun—or any other weapons—to intimidate the residents here.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: No, more than that. You'd best stay in my sight while you're operating in Zwillingstürme.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I'm not aware of any such procedure.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: You mean the rules? Rules are set by people.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I'd like to raise an objection.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Then I'll have to arrest you at the first opportunity, Herr Federico.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: As someone who's fired multiple shots near a noble's private art gallery, many would see you as the biggest threat to Zwillingstürme's order.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: District of Bodenshof, Karl Schmidt Street.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Frieda Seemann, the deceased at the exhibition, resided here for many years.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Right. 'Marigold Alley,' a place beloved by both painters and poets.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Baron Lukas moved here two years ago. He claims he wanted to be closer to an 'increasingly rare artistic milieu,' but of course the real reason might be that the homes here are far cheaper than the ones on Innere Stadt.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I find it very likely that my target has been here before.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Don't be rash. Remember our agreement? Arturia Giallo is a beloved and highly esteemed musician here in Leithanien.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: You're currently 'assisting' the Gendarmerie with an unrelated case, under the premise that whatever you find has nothing to do with me or my men.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I have discovered the alleged gang of violent thugs reported to be disturbing the peace.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Immediately executing—

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Stay put!

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I suggest we immediately initiate arrest procedures.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: It's just a bunch of kids who don't want to attend classes.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Get moving, all of you. No loitering.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: So you were here too. The instrument sculptures were built under the Kaiserinnen's orders, and vandalism will not be tolerated. You're also bothering everyone in the neighborhood with the sound of chiseling.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Still not stopping your Arts?

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: What the hell are you carving?!

steps.name: Stubborn Apprentice
steps.text: Can't you see? I'm just transforming the street back into its proper form.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Twisted horns like those aren't allowed in Zwillingstürme... No, they're forbidden across all of Leithanien.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Step aside. We have to destroy them before the Empresses' Voices find out.

steps.name: Stubborn Apprentice
steps.text: Destroy? What makes you think you're brave enough to destroy a symbol of Herkunftshorn?

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Herkunft— where did you learn that name?

steps.name: Stubborn Apprentice
steps.text: Plenty of people already know. He'll be back soon, after all.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: He was dethroned before you even learned to speak. You have no idea what those horns signify. Back then, he'd erect a sculpture like that on the streets whenever he killed a dissident!

steps.name: Stubborn Apprentice
steps.text: ...Someone's already dead, aren't they?

steps.name: Stubborn Apprentice
steps.text: The painter who lived down the street. She was the first.

steps.name: Stubborn Apprentice
steps.text: Run away with your tail between your legs, meine Herr. Whatever courage you once had is ancient history.

steps.name: Stubborn Apprentice
steps.text: 'The first soldier to set foot in the Witch King's Spire'—do you really think you're still that same hero?

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Don't think I'll let you off just because you hit a nerve, schlingel...

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: He's gone.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Hmph, let him run.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Why did you not arrest him immediately?

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Is there a point in rushing to fill up our prisons?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: May I assume that your reluctance to arrest the boy was due to your personal feelings?

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: ...I'm almost regretting my decision to bring you along, Reverend Executor.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Agreed. Freedom of movement would allow me to lock down the target as soon as possible.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: No, I meant I should have detained you in our office instead.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Why's there another one still here? Hey, junge. Make any more noise and I'll really bring you in.

steps.name: Serene Apprentice
steps.text: ...The twisted horn sculptures. Are you not going to clean them up?

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Right, I still have these troublesome things to deal with. I really don't get what youngsters have in their heads these days.

steps.name: Serene Apprentice
steps.text: They're nostalgic for an era they never got to experience in person. But there's nothing wrong with that. All Leithanians are entitled to feel disappointed with how things are today.

steps.name: Serene Apprentice
steps.text: For example... the coachmen casters who lost their jobs to Victorian automobiles, or the owners of the community theaters that closed down thanks to Wrankwood's film industry. Or their children, of course.

steps.name: Serene Apprentice
steps.text: When people see no way out, the only way they can imagine a future is by looking back at the past.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Hah. Did you hear all that from some adult at home?

steps.name: Serene Apprentice
steps.text: As if. I guarantee you she'd never say anything like that.

steps.name: Serene Apprentice
steps.text: All she knows is how to eliminate any threat to Leithanien at its source.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: The sculpture... shattered? And so easily...

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: He is clearly no ordinary student. I would recommend stopping him for questioning.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Hm. Nothing ordinary about him, that's for sure. But all the more reason to keep our mouths shut.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: ...And now it's actually raining, hah.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Want a drink? Coffee, or maybe beer? If we're drinking at this place, I recommend the former.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I do not make a habit of consuming fluids that will affect my central nervous system while on a mission.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Alright, beer for me then.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: You are also—

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: On a mission, ja. Why else would I be drinking at this hour?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: The child from earlier said that you were 'the first soldier to set foot in the Witch King's Spire.'

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: He's not wrong. What, want me to sign a napkin for you?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I would rather you sign the cooperation agreement I sent you.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Reverend Executor, how old were you twenty-three years ago? The news coverage on the coup can't have been bigger than the ads for some new dessert shop, can they?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: 'The Lateran who became the captain of Zwillingstürme's Gendarmerie.' That's how the headline went.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: You sure did your homework.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I've paid no attention to your ties to the Witch King. The Loris Bordin I read about was a law enforcement officer worth working with, having solved one strange case after another.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Is that why you wrote me so many letters?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Arturia's Arts are unusual, and you are well versed in handling similarly strange cases.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: In the year 1079, you arrested a gang of thieves proficient in casting illusions for romance scams. In 1085, you shot dead a dangerous hypnotist. In—

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Wait. Stop right there. Please don't take me for the protagonist of some detective drama.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: You appear to be avoiding the topic, Loris Bordin.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: And why would I do that? It's just that I accepted early on that I'm a loser.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Did you know? Jan, he... That uncooperative kid we ran into in Marigold Alley earlier, he had a sister who used to work here.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: She went missing fifteen years ago.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Judging by your special treatment of the young man, I assume the case remains unsolved.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: And that's not the only case I haven't been able to crack. Not the first, and definitely not the last.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: There's nothing special about it at all.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: It just... is.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Heh... A Notarial Hall executor like you probably hasn't experienced failure like that.

steps.name: Shopkeeper
steps.text: Herr Bordin! You're here again. How are things lately?

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: The doctor told me to give up drinking.

steps.name: Shopkeeper
steps.text: That's a shame. To make a Lethanian man in his prime cut off his alcohol intake is just as bad as making him go deaf!

steps.name: Shopkeeper
steps.text: I even thought I'd give you a 50% discount if you brought the Damen und Herren from the Gendarmerie here for your retirement party.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: You're retiring?

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: I'm leaving Leithanien once Das Kaiserinnensfest is over.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Thiem, what's that kid been up to lately?

steps.name: Shopkeeper
steps.text: Jan? The Universität he applied to rejected him, so he probably went off to learn a proper trade.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: He's pretty talented with Arts, and his grades in secondary school weren't bad either. So why wasn't he scouted by any of the universities?

steps.name: Shopkeeper
steps.text: Because he threw away your recommendation letter.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: That bengel...

steps.name: Shopkeeper
steps.text: He said you should be trying harder to find Yulia, rather than worrying about which school he's going to.

steps.name: Shopkeeper
steps.text: And also... *sigh* Actually, now that I've gone and said it, I think something's not quite right with the boy lately.

steps.name: Shopkeeper
steps.text: On the day he got your recommendation letter, he asked me why his father didn't need one back in the day. Said he'd entered a certain Graf's spire solely by his own abilities.

steps.name: Shopkeeper
steps.text: 'Talent was more important than lineage back when His Majesty was still around.' His words.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: ...Where exactly has he been hanging out these days?

steps.name: Shopkeeper
steps.text: Not sure.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: The twisted horn sculptures.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: As you implied, Jan shouldn't have even known what they looked like. Which means someone else showed him first.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Oh, right. Which area used to have the highest concentration of those twisted horn sculptures?

steps.name: Shopkeeper
steps.text: Hm, Gustav Park? Not far from here. They call it Forest Park these days.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: You should head home early today, Thiem.

steps.name: Shopkeeper
steps.text: Huh? Sure. Wait, Herr Bordin? Why did you give me your wallet? You could buy a whole year's worth of beer with this much!

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: Keep it. It's for Jan.

steps.name: Loris
steps.text: He's a clever kid, and should go to a good university. That should be enough for him to leave Leithanien and go polish himself in Victoria or Columbia.
The rain stops.
The park fountains do not, not even when the rain was still falling earlier.

There are people sitting or standing under the trees in groups of two of three, most holding an instrument. Violins, flutes, cellos. They seem to be playing independently, but the resulting performance is a harmonious ensemble.
Melodies both soothing and mournful dance on the water and float through the trees.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: When I was a child, I heard that Einwald was a vast stretch of black forest before the nomadic cities were built.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: And whenever someone important passed away, people would go deep into the woods to remember the departed while playing their favorite music.

steps.name: Bereaved Youth
steps.text: I don't see you holding an instrument.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: When I returned to Leithanien, I brought nothing with me.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I used to believe I could play all manner of instruments, but later I met a teacher I respect, who was keen to tell me that I didn't understand the first thing about music.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: But what he meant was... I didn't understand emotions.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Back then, I couldn't comprehend how that was possible. My short life had clearly been brimming with more than enough loss and suffering.

steps.name: Bereaved Youth
steps.text: And then?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: And then... my friend died.

steps.name: Bereaved Youth
steps.text: Then you must have felt true pain.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: To be honest, I'm still not sure I truly understood.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Then I left Leithanien and travelled the lands. I would play for the people I met, and their praise grew only more enthusiastic with every place I visited.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: But I haven't played anything specifically for my dear friend in a long, long time.

steps.name: Bereaved Youth
steps.text: I'm sure they'd love to hear your performance, no matter what level you're at.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I know. And precisely because I know, I hope I can improve.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Have I ever actually tried to stand up to anything in my life?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Can I honestly tell him, with my back straight and my head held high, that I lived a life full enough, rich enough... that it was worthy of his sacrifice?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I can't imagine how he would reply... because I'm not even sure what to say to him in the first place.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: And you, sir? Who do you hold in your heart when you come here?

steps.name: Bereaved Youth
steps.text: A mentor. He left us twenty-three years ago, but I never forgot him.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: He must have been a great man.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I heard that this park was established to commemorate the victims from twenty-three years ago. Every tree standing here replaced a twisted horn sculpture made of flesh and blood.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I have to admire them. During those dark times, they had the courage to stand up and resist fate.

steps.name: Bereaved Youth
steps.text: Perhaps you're the same.

steps.name: Bereaved Youth
steps.text: A lot of the music we listen to is much older than even the entire history of Leithanien. The wills of the departed continue to live on in us, through their music.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Live on in us... Right. I want to believe that.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Do you see that man standing over there?

steps.name: Bereaved Youth
steps.text: You mean... the one carrying a sword, who's been following you?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: That's the one.

steps.name: Bereaved Youth
steps.text: Do you know him?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Serious, calm, lacking emotion.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Their faces always look so alike I don't even bother distinguishing them anymore.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: My time's up, isn't it?

steps.name: Stern Youth
steps.text: ...You certainly enjoy wasting time, 'Graf Urtica.'

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Wunderbar. So I didn't mistake you for someone else.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Truth be told, Herr Overseer, I did think I was ready for you when I first walked into the park.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: 'If Their Majesties want my life, then they can have it.'

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: After all... from then 'til now, and even for the foreseeable future— my life has never truly been a boon to anyone.

steps.name: Stern Youth
steps.text: Did you come here to plan your suicide?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I only considered it for a moment. Besides, if I'd pointed my wand at my throat you'd rush in to stop me, no?

steps.name: Stern Youth
steps.text: The Voice of Mundane has yet to play. So you cannot die.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: What a shame... No matter who I hear that from, it never makes me the slightest bit happy.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Can you hear that cello? I spent the afternoon reviewing my past through the sound of music, and myself on the water's surface.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: And my conclusion? My life really isn't worth any more than it was a few years ago.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: However, just like back then, no one can use it or manipulate it. Especially not—

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: You people.

steps.name: Stern Youth
steps.text: What are you saying—

steps.name: Stern Youth
steps.text: An ambush?!
Several black spheres conjured with Arts leap from the puddles in the area.
They had been camouflaged within the reflections of the trees in the water, and accompanied the melodies drifting through the air as they accumulated energy from the wobbly ripples.

steps.name: Stern Youth
steps.text: —Ugh!

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: So they sent a whole party just to execute me. Would you like me to perform a deep bow in appreciation of Their Majesties?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Sadly, I'm doomed to disappoint them.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I still haven't figured out when I'll play for him.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: But there is one thing I will absolutely tell him myself.

spans.text: one thing I will absolutely tell him myself.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: 'I tried. I was always trying.'

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: 'I never stopped resisting.'
